examples.en: I threw up everything I ate yesterday.
The baby drank milk and then spit up a little.

examples.ko: 차를 오래 타서 속이 안 좋아 결국 게웠어요.
examples.en: I rode in the car for a long time, felt sick, and finally threw up.

examples.ko: 속이 울렁거려서 화장실에서 다 게워 냈어요.
examples.en: My stomach was churning, so I threw it all up in the bathroom.
If your stomach hurts, don't force yourself to throw up.

examples.ko: 너무 많이 먹으면 게울 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat too much, you might throw up.

explain: '토하다'와 같은 상황에 쓰지만 '토하다'가 더 일상적이고, '게우다'는 먹은 것을 입으로 도로 내보낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 'ㅜ'가 '워'로 바뀌어 '게워요, 게웠어요'가 되고, '게워 내다'처럼도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes the same situation as '토하다', but '토하다' is more common in daily speech, while '게우다' feels like bringing back up what you ate. The stem changes to '게워요/게웠어요', and it is often used as '게워 내다'.

examples.en: A headband is convenient when you exercise.

examples.ko: 딸이 분홍색 머리띠를 사 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: My daughter asked me to buy her a pink headband.
My head hurts because of the headband.
I bought a cute headband at the festival.
With a headband on, my bangs don't fall down.
He tied a white band around his forehead.

explain: '머리띠를 하다'가 가장 자연스럽고 '두르다'도 써요. '머리핀'은 머리카락을 고정하는 작은 물건이고, '머리띠'는 머리 둘레를 감는 것이에요. 시험 응원 때 이마에 두르는 천도 '머리띠'라고 해요.
explain_en: '머리띠를 하다' is the most natural, and '두르다' also works. A '머리핀' is a small clip that holds hair, while a '머리띠' wraps around the head. The cloth tied on the forehead to cheer for an exam is also a '머리띠'.

examples.en: The child keeps following me, holding on to my waistband.
Grandfather slipped his hand into his waistband.
Don't walk with your hands in your waistband.
My younger brother's pants keep slipping, so he keeps pulling them up.
The water was deep, so I got wet all the way up to my waist.
A few coins fell out of my waistband.

explain: '허리춤'과 거의 같게 쓰지만 바지의 허리 부분을 가리켜요. '바지춤을 올리다', '바지춤에 손을 넣다'처럼 허리를 잡거나 올리는 동작과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '허리춤' but points to the waist part of pants. It often appears with actions like pulling up the waistband or putting a hand in it, as in '바지춤을 올리다' and '바지춤에 손을 넣다'.

en: to have a safe delivery; to have an easy labor

examples.en: My older sister safely gave birth to a healthy son.
I prayed, hoping for a safe delivery.

examples.ko: 오늘 아침에 친구가 순산해서 병원에 가고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend gave birth safely this morning, so I'm heading to the hospital.
Everyone was happy at the news that she had delivered safely.

examples.ko: 순산하려면 임신 중에 가벼운 운동도 필요하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say light exercise during pregnancy is needed for an easy delivery.
The baby will be here soon. I hope the delivery goes well!

explain: 아기를 큰 문제 없이 낳았다는 뜻이라서 '출산하다'보다 축하하고 걱정해 주는 느낌이 있어요. 임신한 사람에게 '순산하세요'라고 인사하고, 소식을 전할 때는 '순산했어요', 높일 때는 '순산하셨어요'라고 해요.
explain_en: Because it means giving birth without major trouble, it carries a congratulatory, caring tone that '출산하다' lacks. People greet a pregnant woman with '순산하세요', and say '순산했어요' when sharing news, or '순산하셨어요' to be respectful.

en: to be tingling; to be stinging

examples.ko: 겨울 아침 찬 공기를 마시면 코가 싸해요.
examples.en: When I breathe the cold winter morning air, my nose stings.

examples.ko: 매운 겨자를 먹자 코끝이 싸하게 아팠어요.
examples.en: After eating hot mustard, the tip of my nose tingled painfully.
There was a smell of disinfectant and my nose stung.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣는 순간 가슴이 싸해졌어요.
examples.en: The moment I heard that, my heart sank with a stinging feeling.

examples.ko: 찬바람 때문에 목이 싸할 때는 따뜻한 차를 마셔요.
examples.en: When my throat stings from the cold wind, I drink warm tea.

examples.ko: 속이 싸해서 물을 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: My stomach stung, so I drank a glass of water.

explain: 코, 목, 속, 가슴이 소독약이나 찬 기운, 매운 것 때문에 아린 느낌이에요. '화하다'는 시원하게 퍼지는 느낌이고, '싸하다'는 아리고 쓰린 느낌이 더 있어요. 마음이 서늘하게 아플 때 '가슴이 싸하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a stinging, sharp feeling in the nose, throat, stomach or chest from disinfectant, cold air or spicy food. '화하다' feels cool and spreading, while '싸하다' has more of a stinging, smarting feel. People also say '가슴이 싸하다' when the heart aches with a chill.

en: wide open; with a crack or smack; tightly (sticking)

examples.en: I yawned with my mouth wide open.
I split the watermelon in half with a knife.
The drought was long, so the rice paddy ground cracked wide open.
The wet clothes clung tightly to my body.

examples.ko: 어깨가 쩍 벌어진 남자가 문 앞에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A broad-shouldered man was standing at the door.

examples.ko: 아이가 쩍 소리가 나게 입맛을 다셨어요.
examples.en: The child smacked his lips with a loud sound.

explain: 입이나 틈이 크게 벌어지거나, 붙어 있던 것이 갈라지고 달라붙는 느낌을 나타내요. '쩍 벌어지다, 쩍 갈라지다, 쩍 달라붙다'처럼 정해진 동사와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 소리를 흉내 낼 때도 써요.

phrases.en: My jaw dropped when I heard the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 놀라서 말이 안 나올 때 써요. 실제로 입을 벌렸는지와 상관없이 크게 놀랐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so amazed you cannot speak. It does not need an actual open mouth; it just means you were greatly astonished.

explain_en: It conveys the feel of something opening wide, splitting, or sticking firmly. It usually pairs with set verbs such as '쩍 벌어지다', '쩍 갈라지다' and '쩍 달라붙다'. It can also imitate a smacking sound.

examples.en: After eating a mint candy, my mouth feels cool and minty.

examples.ko: 치약 맛이 너무 화해서 아이가 싫어해요.
examples.en: The toothpaste is so minty that my child doesn't like it.

examples.ko: 파스를 붙이니 처음에는 화하다가 곧 따뜻해졌어요.
examples.en: When I put on the patch it first felt cooling, then soon warm.

examples.ko: 화한 느낌 때문에 껌을 자주 씹어요.
examples.en: I chew gum often because of the cooling sensation.

examples.ko: 박하 향이 화하게 퍼져서 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: The mint scent spread sharply and woke me up.

examples.ko: 코가 화할 만큼 시원한 바람이 불었어요.
examples.en: A breeze so cool it made my nose tingle blew by.

explain: 박하, 민트, 파스처럼 입, 코, 피부에 시원하게 퍼지는 느낌이에요. '시원하다'보다 감각이 더 구체적이에요. '화(怒)'와 상관없는 말이니 '화해요'를 '화가 나요'로 오해하지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes a cooling sensation spreading through the mouth, nose or skin, as with mint or a medicated patch. It is more specific than '시원하다'. It has nothing to do with '화' (anger), so don't mistake '화해요' for '화가 나요'.

examples.en: That actor is tall and handsome.

examples.ko: 훤칠한 청년이 가게 문을 열고 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A tall, good-looking young man opened the shop door and came in.
My son has grown up tall and good-looking, and it's nice to see.
I heard the groom is tall and handsome, and has a good personality too.

examples.ko: 새로 온 선생님은 훤칠해서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The new teacher stands out because he's tall and good-looking.

examples.ko: 저는 훤칠하지는 않아도 인상이 좋다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: I may not be tall and striking, but people say I have a good impression.

explain: 키가 크면서 모습이 시원스럽고 보기 좋을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '후리후리하다'는 키 크고 날씬한 몸을 말하고, '훤칠하다'는 거기에 잘생긴 느낌까지 더해져요. 주로 사람에게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for someone who is tall and looks clean-cut and pleasing. '후리후리하다' describes a tall, slim body, while '훤칠하다' adds a handsome feel. It is used mainly for people.
